edbDesc: The emission of short bursts of light from imploding bubbles in a liquid when excited by sound.
title: Sonoluminescence
description: Tiny bubbles in water blasted with loud ultrasound collapse so violently that they flash with light. Frenzel and Schultes at Cologne found it when photographic plates in an ultrasound bath came out fogged, and today the glow is used to map where cavitation is strongest in ultrasonic cleaners and chemical reactors.
effect: collapsing bubbles in sound-driven water give off flashes of light
usedIn: Mapping cavitation in ultrasonic cleaning tanks
Studying extreme temperatures inside collapsing bubbles
strength: The light is faint, a pale blue glow visible only in a dark room, but each flash lasts under a billionth of a second and the gas inside may reach about 10,000 degrees.
pickWhy: Borderline: Specific named effect, but the light is weak and its uses are mostly diagnostic; I kept it because it reveals extreme conditions made with tabletop sound.
